Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Summary: A Vision for National Renewal

This manifesto presents a comprehensive plan for national transformation, arguing that the country has experienced 14 years of instability, declining public services, and broken promises. The document outlines five core missions and detailed policy proposals across multiple sectors.

## Core Principles and Foundations

The manifesto establishes three non-negotiable foundations: national security, secure borders, and economic stability. It commits to maintaining nuclear deterrence, NATO membership, and conducting a Strategic Defence Review. On borders, it proposes a new Border Security Command to combat people-smuggling networks while clearing asylum backlogs. Economic stability is underpinned by strict fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt as a share of GDP.

## Economic Growth Strategy

The central economic argument is that sustainable growth requires government acting as a strategic partner with business rather than standing aside. Key proposals include:

- An Industrial Strategy Council on statutory footing
- A National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion to attract private investment
- Planning reform to enable 1.5 million new homes
- Business rates reform to support high streets
- A ten-year infrastructure strategy
- Bringing railways into public ownership as contracts expire
- Skills England to coordinate workforce development
- A "New Deal for Working People" including banning exploitative zero-hours contracts and strengthening worker rights

## Clean Energy Transition

The manifesto sets an ambitious target of clean power by 2030, positioning this as both an economic opportunity and security imperative. Central to this is Great British Energy, a new publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, capitalised with £8.3 billion. The plan includes doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind capacity. A Warm Homes Plan would invest £6.6 billion to upgrade five million homes. The document commits to no new oil and gas exploration licences while managing existing fields responsibly.

## Public Safety and Justice

The manifesto aims to halve serious violent crime and violence against women and girls within a decade. Proposals include a Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands of new officers, specialist rape units in every police force, and a Young Futures programme to prevent youth crime. It promises to address the prison crisis, reduce reoffending, and introduce a "Hillsborough Law" requiring candour from public servants.

## Education and Opportunity

Breaking the link between background and success is framed as a defining mission. Proposals include 6,500 new teachers, free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, 3,000 new primary school-based nurseries, and curriculum reform. The document commits to ending VAT exemptions for private schools to fund state education improvements. Further education would be transformed through Skills England and specialist Technical Excellence Colleges.

## Health and Social Care

The NHS mission focuses on reform alongside investment, shifting toward prevention and community-based care. Immediate priorities include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, and recruiting 8,500 mental health staff. A Dentistry Rescue Plan would provide 700,000 urgent appointments. The document commits to developing a National Care Service with national standards and a Fair Pay Agreement for social care workers.

## Constitutional and Democratic Reform

Proposals include establishing an Ethics and Integrity Commission, modernising Commons procedures, removing hereditary peers, and introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for Lords members. The manifesto commits to votes at 16 and strengthening relationships with devolved governments through a new Council of the Nations and Regions.

## International Relations

The document emphasises rebuilding alliances while remaining outside the EU single market and customs union. It proposes seeking improved trade arrangements with Europe, maintaining the US special relationship, and creating a Clean Power Alliance for climate action. Development spending would return to 0.7% of GNI when fiscal circumstances allow.

## Funding

The fiscal plan identifies revenue from closing tax loopholes (non-dom status, carried interest, private equity), extending windfall taxes on oil and gas companies, and efficiency savings including halving consultancy spending. The Green Prosperity Plan would be funded partly through windfall taxes and partly through borrowing within fiscal rules.

# Summary of Policy Document

This document outlines a comprehensive policy platform addressing multiple areas of governance, public services, and economic reform.

## Immigration and Border Control

The platform proposes freezing non-essential immigration while maintaining exceptions for healthcare workers. It advocates for offshore processing of asylum seekers, immediate deportation of foreign nationals who commit crimes, restrictions on student dependents, and a five-year residency requirement before accessing benefits. An employer tax of 20% on foreign workers is proposed to incentivise hiring domestic workers.

## Economic Policy

**Personal taxation** proposals include raising the income tax threshold to £20,000 annually, reducing fuel duty by 20p per litre, eliminating VAT on energy bills, cutting stamp duty on properties below £750,000, and abolishing inheritance tax for estates under £2 million.

**Business measures** include exempting businesses with profits under £100,000 from corporation tax, reducing the main corporation tax rate to 15% over time, raising the VAT threshold to £150,000, abolishing business rates for high street enterprises, and introducing a 4% online delivery tax for large multinational companies.

## Public Services

**Healthcare** reforms focus on eliminating waiting lists through tax incentives for medical staff, utilising independent healthcare capacity, providing 20% tax relief on private healthcare, and implementing a voucher system allowing patients to access private treatment when NHS waiting times exceed specified limits.

**Policing and Justice** proposals include recruiting 40,000 new officers, implementing zero-tolerance policing, mandatory life sentences for repeat violent offenders, building 10,000 new detention places, and reopening local magistrates' courts.

**Education** reforms propose curriculum changes emphasising national heritage, banning gender ideology teaching in schools, providing 20% tax relief on independent education, and scrapping interest on student loans.

## Energy and Environment

The platform advocates abandoning net-zero targets, scrapping renewable energy subsidies, fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licensing, exploring shale gas extraction, and developing nuclear energy through small modular reactors.

## Defence and Veterans

Proposals include increasing defence spending to 3% of GDP within six years, conducting an urgent military pay review, creating a dedicated veterans ministry, recruiting 30,000 full-time army personnel, and reforming defence procurement.

## Housing and Infrastructure

Housing measures include fast-tracking brownfield development, prioritising local residents for social housing, scrapping certain landlord tax restrictions, and protecting leaseholders. Infrastructure proposals include cancelling a major rail project, banning urban traffic restriction zones, and creating a new ownership model bringing 50% of utilities into public ownership.

## Agriculture and Fishing

Agricultural policy proposes increasing the farming budget to £3 billion, eliminating climate-related farming subsidies, and targeting 70% domestic food sourcing. Fishing reforms include ending automatic EU access to UK waters, requiring foreign vessels to purchase licences, and banning foreign supertrawlers.

## Constitutional and Social Reforms

Proposals include withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights, reforming the upper legislative chamber, restricting postal voting, considering proportional representation, replacing equality legislation, and reforming the national broadcaster's funding model.

## Financial Summary

The document claims potential annual savings of £150 billion through reduced government spending, benefit reforms, and energy policy changes, plus £10 billion from projected economic growth. Proposed spending increases total £141 billion annually, covering tax cuts, public services, and defence.
